messages:
maria: heads-up — after r3172 deploy we're seeing a memory "ripple" across kv slabs in prod10. not full OOMs but a lot of longctx allocations staying resident. p50 mem ~+7%, p99 ~+40%. observability: https://perf.redwood/prod10/kv/r3172

ben: which hosts / pods? logs?

maria: mainly gpu-pool-3 nodes (gpu3-*) and a couple in gpu-pool-1. attaching quick pmap snapshot from one host:
```
PID   RSS
12345 6.4G
12346 6.1G
12347 7.9G  <-- process serving longctx workloads
```
pattern: RSS climbs in ~10-30s windows, then drops, repeat — looks like fragmentation/stripe growth rather than a single leak.

kai: any recent changes touching batching or allocation? last deploy had the batching padding heuristic + kernel-routing fallback change. those touched the allocator hotpath.

maria: yes, r3172 included batching change to reduce padding (commit 5f8c6e7) and kernel fallback reassign (commit 2b9d3a1). perf CI didn't flag anything big but the smoke perf run on canary showed a small p99 mem delta (~+12%) but was under threshold so auto-rollout continued.

alex: can you share perf flamegraph and kv slab histograms?

maria: flamegraph (short): https://perf.redwood/fg/r3172-prod10 — shows a new hotspot in kv::alloc_strided (the stride allocator path) called from autobatch::pad_chunks. histogram: slab sizes 256/512/768 growing; large (>1MB) object count unchanged.

ben: that points to stride allocation pattern causing fragmentation. maybe the new padding produced many odd-sized allocations that fragmented slabs. worth bisecting the two commits.

maria: started quick git bisect locally, reproducer is the microbench harness we use for longctx heavy traces. commands: 
```
git bisect start origin/main r3150
git bisect bad r3172
git bisect good r3150
# test harness: ./bench/kv_stride_repro --trace traces/longctx.json
```

kai: i can run a cluster bisect job. triggering now.

deploy-bot: ci: queued cluster-bisect job #3921 for kv-stride-repro on prod-like pool.

jen: I'm going to pause rollout for prod10 and prod11 until we have root cause, setting rollout-hold on canary group.

maria: thanks. quick local bisect narrowed it to the batching padding commit (5f8c6e7). when I revert just the padding change locally the reproduction stops.

alex: great find. can you paste the small repro log?

maria: repro log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] bench: started trace longctx.json
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] kv: alloc_strided size=384 -> slab=512 idx=7
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] kv: alloc_strided size=128 -> slab=256 idx=3
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] kv: free idx=3 (slow)
[2026-03-18T09:12:25Z] kv: alloc_strided size=384 -> slab=768 idx=11
[2026-03-18T09:12:25Z] kv: slab_frag_mult 1.38
```
shows interleaved small-medium allocations causing fragmentation multiplier to climb.

ben: did we change the stride alignment or group size? the padding heuristic reduced pad to nearest 64 bytes; old behavior rounded to 128. that could create more mixed sizes.

kai: yes, batching.patch (5f8c6e7) moved pad to 64 to save tokens. on avg it's better but when hitting longctx with many similar seq-lens it produces many 384/448 sized allocations instead of uniform 512, so slabs don't pack well.

alex: two paths forward: 1) revert padding change for now (fast). 2) implement subtle coalescing in allocator to prefer canonical sizes (slower). also add a perf test covering this scenario.

maria: opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4291 — revert batching pad reduction. adding regression test in bench/kv_stride_repro.

jen: rolled back r3172 for prod10 and prod11 to r3158 as an emergency rollback. alerting CS and oncall.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback r3172 -> r3158 initiated for clusters: prod10, prod11.

ben: good. we should also add telemetry for slab fragmentation and an alert if slab_frag_mult > 1.2 for 5m.

maria: agree — adding observability ticket and radar. also flagging kernel-routing team; fallback paths may change allocation ordering and amplify this.

kai: +1 on alarm. i'll add a CI perf test that runs bench/kv_stride_repro under a memory frag checker and fails if p99 mem delta > 8%.

alex: please include a comment in PR 4291 linking to this thread and to the flamegraph and bisect notes. once revert merges we can iterate on allocator coalesce, probably avoid full revert if we can implement bucket-normalization in allocator.

maria: putting postmortem notes in #incidents and will follow up with a short write-up: root cause = batching pad reduction -> more mixed allocation sizes -> slab fragmentation spikes under longctx heavy workloads. mitigation = rollback + add fragment telemetry + CI regression.

jen: thanks all. quick checklist:
- [x] rollout paused for affected clusters
- [x] rollback r3172 -> r3158 prod10/11
- [x] revert PR opened (#4291)
- [ ] allocator coalesce design (alex/kai)
- [ ] CI regression added (kai)
- [ ] slab fragmentation alert (ben)

maria: i'll keep monitoring, will post updates here as PRs land. :thumbsup:
